central_unknown: Extreme heat at the Red Bull Ring creates massive reliability uncertainty across the grid, particularly for Cadillac (both cars DNF risk), Mercedes (engine heat management concerns), and Red Bull (FP1 issues). Whether Ferrari's ADUO engine upgrade closes the gap to Mercedes on this power-sensitive circuit is also a key unknown.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Consensus pick across all channels. Looked far and away the fastest in FP2, dominant on Friday. Even when he doesn't win, he consistently scores high points. Best 2x boost option by wide margin.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lewis Hamilton
captains.reason: ZachGP mentions him as differential for upcoming Silverstone (home GP, Driver of the Day potential), but multiple channels note Ferrari didn't look close to Mercedes in Austria FP sessions. Better saved for Silverstone as 2x option.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: At price floor (3M), cannot lose value. 82% ownership in global top 500. Must-have budget enabler. Audi reliability improving. Needs 21 pts for price rise so will stay cheap, but safe floor of points when he finishes.

buy.name: Isack Hadjar
buy.note: Strong consensus pick. Top-8 finishes recently, 15 pts in Barcelona, needs only ~3 pts for max price rise. FanAmp and ZachGP both rate him highly. Some FP1 concerns about Red Bull reliability in heat but clear-cut favorite premium B-tier driver.

buy.name: Arvid Lindblad
buy.note: Best value asset in the game. 28 points over last 2 races (14/race avg). Needs only -12 pts for min price rise, -7 for max. 49% top-500 ownership. Preferred over Bortoleto for budget building this week.

buy.name: Pierre Gasly
buy.note: Monaco points adjustment boosted his 3-race average to 25 pts. Alpine reliability is excellent. FanAmp prefers Gasly over Hadjar due to reliability. Needs only -9 pts for 0.2 rise. Strong hold if already owned.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Good hold, not a priority buy. Racing Bulls looked fast (P9 in FP2). Needs 2 pts for min price rise, 10 for max. Multiple channels say fine to hold but luxury transfer to exit. Better long-term once Barcelona DNF drops off average.

consider.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
consider.note: Consistent 5-7 point floor but lacks upside for max price rise. Slightly worse budget builder than Lindblad this week. Fine hold but Lindblad preferred if choosing between them.

consider.name: Oliver Bearman
consider.note: ZachGP mentions as differential pick. Haas is reliable. Only 1 pt in last race but needs just 11 pts for 0.2 rise. Risky but has upside if Haas pace returns.

avoid: Valtteri Bottas — Three consecutive mechanical DNFs. Cadillac reliability is terrible. 44% implied DNF probability per betting odds. Even at 3M floor price, not worth the -50 risk until he proves he can finish a race.
Lance Stroll — 49% implied DNF probability. Aston Martin reliability dire. Will continue losing value. Avoid unless absolutely needed for 4A.

Franco Colapinto — FanAmp says time to sell. Needs 18 pts to avoid price drop which is unlikely. Has gained 0.6M six straight races but regression coming. DNF risk increasing. Multiple channels moving off him.
Sergio Perez — Cadillac stopped on track in both FP1 and FP2. 6.2M is too expensive for the DNF risk. Multiple channels explicitly warn against him despite tempting price rise thresholds.
Esteban Ocon — Slower Haas driver, many better options at his price point.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: Not recommended for Austria. ZachGP covers chips in separate video but F1FantasyPolePosition notes 4 straight mode zones mean high overtakes, which doesn't particularly favor Limitless. Save for a sprint weekend or more favorable track.

chips.name: No Negative
chips.reason: F1FantasyPolePosition suggests this might be the right weekend given extreme heat and reliability concerns across the grid. Both Cadillacs struggling, multiple cars on 'high stands of doom' during Friday practice. High DNF risk weekend.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: No channel recommends using Wildcard this weekend. Better saved for the pivot into 4A lineups in 2-3 races.

chips.name: 3x Captain (Triple Captain)
chips.reason: ReinFantasy's video title suggests using 3x at Silverstone (sprint weekend next week) rather than Austria. Sprint weekends offer more scoring opportunities for captain multiplier.

watch_items: Ferrari ADUO engine upgrade: Could add ~15 HP but didn't look close to Mercedes in Friday practice. Monitor FP3 for improvement.

Mercedes heat reliability: Battery upgrades and bigger cooling louvers brought to Austria, but extreme 34°C temperatures on Sunday remain a concern. George Russell's car was worked on at start of FP2.
Red Bull reliability: Both Verstappen and Hadjar had FP1 issues. Hadjar was on radio saying he's not at one with the car after updates. Monitor Saturday closely.
McLaren as constructor alternative: Piastri and Norris looked strong in FP2, close to Mercedes. But Norris had hydraulics leak in FP1 and cannot run upgraded Mercedes battery without engine penalty.
Gasly Monaco appeal: Still active appeals on Gasly's P3 podium. Could see another retroactive scoring change affecting Gasly, Hadjar, Lawson, Lindblad, and Piastri price calculations.
Lando Norris at engine component limit: Would take grid penalty if he needs a new battery, making McLaren constructor riskier.
arc: Austria kicks off a double-header with Silverstone (sprint weekend) the following week. The consensus is to resist the urge to pivot to 4A lineups now — most channels recommend waiting 2-3 more races until budgets reach ~120M, which allows running 4A without needing both Bottas and Stroll as dead weight. The target 4A team is Antonelli, Hamilton, Lindblad, Bortoleto, Hulkenberg, Mercedes, Ferrari at ~120.7M. For now, maximize budget building through Hadjar/Gasly, Lindblad, and Hulkenberg. Silverstone next week is a sprint weekend where Hamilton becomes a strong 2x/3x differential at his home GP, and the 3x captain chip is being recommended for that race. The key strategic tension is whether to hold Gasly or swap to Hadjar — both are excellent but Hadjar has slightly better long-term budget trajectory while Gasly has better reliability backing from Alpine.
